summary: 1949 Maine Forest Service 60-foot Aermotor tower on Mount Pisgah; retired 1991-92, now town-owned with a land trust easement and open to the public.

facts.agency: Town of Winthrop, Maine (owner); built by Maine Forest Service

access.note: Tower property is 94 acres, owned by the Town of Winthrop and protected with a Kennebec Land Trust easement. The Land Trust and the register describe the tower as open to the public.

visit.trail_note: Tower Trail: 0.7 mile moderate trail from a Land Trust parking lot on Mt. Pisgah Road

events.note: Maine Forest Service constructed the 60-foot tower with a 7x7 cab
Land Trust says the tower was in use from 1949 to 1991
Forest Lookouts summary records the lookout as de-commissioned in 1992
By August 2008 the Town of Winthrop owned the tower, managed jointly with the Kennebec Land Trust, which holds a conservation easement
Vandals ripped a safety rail from around the cab's entry hole

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Kennebec Land Trust says the tower was in use from 1949 to 1991. The Forest Lookouts summary records decommissioning in 1992. The story reports both dates and does not pick one.
The Forest Lookouts summary calls the tower steel; the register names it an Aermotor tower. Both fit the same structure, so the story uses both descriptions.

notes_for_editor: Access 'public' comes from the Land Trust and the register; the story gives no climbing advice. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Maine Facebook snippet says the tower was used as a radio tower around 1995 and was not then generally open to the public. It was not fetched, so the story leaves it out. The 2008 Morning Sentinel item is quoted through the Forest Lookouts page and was not read directly. No staffing history or notable fires were found, so those keys are omitted.
